compensating.why: hop 1 answers a watch that has no start mark with 0
hop 2 passes a stop mark below zero as 0
hop 3 counts a watch as live only once it has a start mark
hop 4 never returns a time below zero

ownership_reason: Only the gold computes the time on the watch: the recorded part from the start mark to the stop mark (never less than zero) and, while the watch is live, the part from the last mark the watch passed to the current time; hops 1-4 pass the start mark, the stop mark and the live flag along unchanged, and the facade only gathers the two private marks and compares the private running state with STATE_RUNNING. The gold's javadoc promises the time from the start mark to the current time while the watch is live, which now + 1 is not for a running watch without a split mark. The convention that a running watch without a stop mark is timed from its start mark is pinned outside the gold: StopWatch.unsplit ('clears the stop time. The start time is unaffected, enabling timing from the original start point to continue'), StopWatch.start (stopTime = -1 when a timing session starts) and StopWatch.resume (stopTime = -1 once the start time is moved on), with StopWatchTest testStopWatchSplit (after unsplit the total runs from the original start, 1500-1900 ms), testStopWatchSuspend and testLang315 passing. The gold and every hop take the start and stop marks 'as the watch recorded' them, and the facade passes the two fields themselves, so the stop mark that reaches the gold for a running watch without a split is the recorded one; a method above the gold that hands down another value in its place (for example the start mark) no longer uses the next method as documented, and no one-line change of the flag above the gold restores the time while staying consistent with the documentation.
